card.name: Hojagiri
card.era: Traditional; evolved from the ritual Hodagiri
card.tagline: Reang women's balancing dance on earthen pitchers
card.profile: Hojagiri is a folk dance of the Reang (Bru) clan of the Tripuri people of Tripura, performed by a team of four to six women and young girls who sing while balancing on earthen pitchers and managing props - a bottle on the head, an earthen lamp in the hand - moving only the lower half of the body (Wikipedia; Prepp). It is danced during the Hojagiri festival (Mailuma/Laxmi Puja) on the full-moon night after Durga Puja, honouring goddess Mailuma (Lakshmi) for a good harvest. Men sing the lyrics and play the kham drum and sumui flute. Dancers wear the handwoven pachra and rea with coin necklaces and silver ornaments (Historified; The Northeast Today).
card.insight: Folk artist Satyaram Reang (1943-2023), who dedicated his life to the dance and ran a Hojagiri school, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1986) and the Padma Shri (2021) for preserving the form (Wikipedia: Satyaram Reang).
